summary.text: Democrat Deb Haaland won the election for governor of New Mexico on November 3, 2026, defeating Greggory Hull, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
An enrolled member of the Pueblo of Laguna, she served as U.S. Secretary of the Interior from 2021 to 2025 and as U.S. Representative for New Mexico's 1st District from 2019 to 2021.

paragraphs.text: Haaland earned a B.A. in English from the University of New Mexico in 1994 and a J.D. from the UNM School of Law in 2006.
As a single mother, she started a salsa company.
She chaired the Democratic Party of New Mexico from 2015 to 2017 and was the party's 2014 nominee for lieutenant governor.
Haaland was elected to Congress in 2018 as one of the first two Native American women in the U.S. House, and the Senate confirmed her as Interior Secretary on March 15, 2021, by a vote of 51–40.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election for Governor of New Mexico with 57.4% of the vote to Greggory Hull's 42.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
